panels.head: Amazon wants to beam satellite connectivity straight to your phone
panels.sub: A new FCC filing reveals plans for a 5,100+ satellite constellation targeting direct-to-device (D2D) service — no special hardware required on the ground.

panels.head: Globalstar spectrum is the key ingredient
panels.sub: Amazon's application leans on Globalstar's licensed spectrum bands, signalling a spectrum-access strategy rather than building a new frequency allocation from scratch.

panels.head: 5,100+ satellites is a serious orbital commitment
panels.sub: That count would place the constellation in the same league as Starlink's current deployment. Amazon already has its Kuiper broadband constellation in progress, so this would be a separate D2D layer — though the filing details remain thin at this stage.

panels.head: D2D is getting crowded fast
panels.sub: SpaceX's Starlink D2D (via T-Mobile) and AST SpaceMobile are already in early commercial operation. Apple-backed Globalstar supplies the SOS link on iPhones. Amazon entering sharpens a race where spectrum rights, not just satellite count, will decide winners.

panels.head: Watch for the Kuiper + D2D bundling play
panels.sub: If Amazon pairs broadband Kuiper with a D2D layer, it could offer end-to-end connectivity for edge devices and remote assets — relevant for logistics, field operations, and IoT deployments that today rely on patchy terrestrial coverage. FCC approval timeline is the next milestone to track.

cards.title: Rocket Lab Opens Alaska Site in $266M Space Force Deal

panels.head: $266M to launch from Kodiak
panels.sub: Space Force is paying Rocket Lab to open a new launch facility in Alaska, one of its largest single contracts to date.

panels.head: Why Alaska?
panels.sub: Kodiak's high-latitude location enables polar and sun-synchronous orbits not easily accessible from Rocket Lab's existing New Zealand and Virginia pads — useful for surveillance and reconnaissance payloads.

panels.head: Up to 18 suborbital missions on the manifest
panels.sub: The contract covers suborbital test missions supporting military hypersonics and other defense R&D programs, not orbital satellite delivery. Cadence and timeline beyond that were not disclosed.

panels.head: Rocket Lab diversifying beyond commercial smallsat launches
panels.sub: Defense contracts now sit alongside commercial Electron missions and the coming Neutron rocket — reducing revenue concentration risk while funding infrastructure Rocket Lab couldn't justify on commercial demand alone.

panels.head: A template for dual-use launch economics
panels.sub: Government anchor tenants funding new pads mirrors how early AWS contracts underwrote cloud infrastructure. Watch whether Kodiak gets opened to commercial polar-orbit customers once the military manifest is established.
